title: Codeplugger radio capabilities
description: Describes what a target radio can physically accept. Scoped to facts a generator needs in order to decide whether a profile will fit and work on the radio, not to model the radio's full feature set.

id.description: Stable radio identifier; must match the containing directory name.

limits.description: Hard structural limits enforced against a resolved profile.

max_channels.description: Total channels the radio can store.

max_zones.description: Zones the radio can store. 0 means the radio has no zone concept.

max_channels_per_zone.description: Channels a single zone can hold.

max_scan_lists.description: Scan lists the radio can store. Omit when unknown.

max_channels_per_scan_list.description: Channels a single scan list can hold. This is the on-radio storage capacity, which may be smaller than the count a CPS UI appears to offer. Omit when unknown.

max_rx_group_lists.description: DMR RX group lists the radio can store. Omit when unknown.

max_talkgroups_per_rx_group_list.description: Talkgroups a single DMR RX group list can hold. Omit when unknown.

max_contacts.description: Contacts the radio can store. Omit when unknown.

max_dmr_ids.description: Distinct DMR radio IDs the radio can store.

max_channel_name_chars.description: Characters a channel display name can hold. Names longer than this may be silently truncated by the CPS or on-radio encoder rather than rejected. Omit when unknown.

max_zone_name_chars.description: Characters a zone name can hold. Omit when unknown.

max_scan_list_name_chars.description: Characters a scan list name can hold. Omit when unknown.

max_contact_name_chars.description: Characters a contact name can hold. Omit when unknown.

firmware_limits.description: Per-firmware limit overrides. Keys are firmware version strings as reported by the radio (e.g. "DM32.01.01.049"). A profile validated without a known firmware uses `limits` intersected with every override here, so an unknown firmware cannot validate against a capacity no shipped firmware provides.

bands.description: Frequency ranges the radio can tune, in MHz. A channel whose RX or TX frequency falls outside every listed band cannot work on this radio. Omit when unknown; validation is then skipped rather than assumed.

rx_only.description: Radio can receive but not transmit in this range (e.g. a broadcast or airband RX span).

modes.description: Channel modes the radio supports. Omit when unknown; validation is then skipped.

bandwidths_khz.description: Analog FM channel bandwidths the radio supports, in kHz. Omit when unknown; validation is then skipped.

notes.description: Free-form provenance or caveats, e.g. where the figures were sourced.

chirp.description: How the `chirp-writer` backend addresses this radio. Omit for radios CHIRP cannot program; the backend then refuses rather than guessing a driver.

driver.description: CHIRP driver name, as printed by `chirp-writer --list-drivers`.

model.description: The 'Vendor Model' string that driver reports. The backend refuses to write when the connected radio reports anything else. This is often not the name on the case: an FT-270R reports as a Yaesu VX-170.

clone_mode.description: `on_demand` means the radio answers whenever the cable is connected. `manual` means an operator must put it into clone mode by hand for every read and write, so the backend runs the helper interactively instead of capturing its output.
clone_mode.$comment: This decides whether a write can be scripted unattended, which is why it lives in capabilities rather than in a profile.

driver_upstream.description: False when the driver is not in released CHIRP yet and must come from a checkout or patch.

benlink.description: How the `benlink` backend reaches and identifies this radio over the Benshi BLE/RFCOMM protocol. Present only for Benshi-protocol radios (Vero VR-N76, BTECH UV-Pro and relatives), which have no programming cable and no CHIRP driver. Omit for every other radio; the backend then refuses rather than guessing a transport.

device_name.description: Substring of the name the radio advertises over Bluetooth, used to find it during discovery. Case-insensitive.

vendor_id.description: `vendor_id` from the device's own GetDeviceInfo reply. Read it from the radio; do not copy it from a spec sheet.

product_id.description: `product_id` from GetDeviceInfo. The backend refuses to write when the connected radio reports anything else, which is the strongest protection available against programming the wrong Benshi-family HT. Absent means never read from hardware, and the backend falls back to the weaker region and channel count check.
product_id.$comment: Optional rather than required because a radio entry can legitimately exist before anyone has connected one; the count check still gates those.

transport.description: `rfcomm` is Linux-only (CPython on macOS has no AF_BLUETOOTH) but survives long write sessions. `ble` works on macOS but needs a bonded link created by a foreground GUI process, so it cannot be driven from a daemon or an SSH session.
transport.$comment: This is a property of how the host must reach the radio, not a user preference, which is why it lives in capabilities.

zone_model.description: Benshi radios partition channels into regions: channel IDs restart at 0 inside each region, so a codeplugger zone is a region and there is no shared global channel pool.

hardware_verified.description: True only once a codeplug has actually been written to this model and read back clean. The backend refuses to program a radio marked false unless the caller explicitly opts in, because the identity gate over Bluetooth is weak: a self-reported product_id at best, and region and channel counts otherwise.
hardware_verified.$comment: Benshi family members share one protocol, so an untested model will appear to work right up until a field means something else on it.

verified_firmware_version.description: Firmware version of the unit these limits were actually read from, as reported by GetDeviceInfo. Limits are per-unit on this family, so this records what was measured rather than what is claimed.

firmwareLimitOverrides.description: Limit overrides for one firmware version. Same keys as `limits`; only the keys that actually change need to be listed. Values replace the base `limits` value, they do not merge per-key.
